steps.what: Review the student's work and decide the recommendation's claims and examples
Write the recommendation letter from verified examples and the teacher's assessment

loop.output: Letter draft with each evaluative claim traced to the brief
loop.check: Teacher checks that tone, strength of endorsement and examples express their actual assessment
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsupported claims require manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot express individual examples and nuanced endorsement

steps.what: Check, sign and send the final recommendation to its intended recipient

tasks.design: Use a bounded drafting tool in {DOCS} only after the teacher chooses the claims and evidence. The teacher corrects, signs and sends the exact final letter through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Individual wording takes time after the academic assessment is complete.
tasks.enabler_now: A draft can be constrained to a small teacher-authored brief.
tasks.still_hard: Confidentiality and the strength of a personal endorsement cannot be delegated.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher knows the student and stands behind every claim.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft work; endorsement rights stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: A teacher-reviewed recommendation draft from supplied examples is plausible; the digest has no recommendation-letter capability or time study establishing this saving.

assumptions: Boundary includes personal assessment, drafting and sending, excluding the recipient's selection decision.

Teacher produces student name, purpose, recipient, verified examples, endorsement strength and permitted disclosures in s1; its full 40 hours includes capture. Missing evidence goes to manual writing in s2.
Test existing document templates before adding a model; no confidential work is uploaded without approved access.
research_questions: Do corrected drafts preserve the teacher's intended endorsement without extra review?

incremental.description: Review instructions, disclosure rules and recurring draft errors

approvals.approved_version: Exact signed letter, attachments and recipient; any content or address change requires fresh approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=40+21+25=86; gross 14 less 4 upkeep gives net 10. Low assumes personal rewriting erases drafting gains and the add-on is not adopted; high requires 40% less first-draft effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select and obtain textbooks and teaching supplies

steps.what: Select textbooks and supplies after reviewing teaching fit, editions and availability
Enter selected material identifiers and quantities into a purchase request
Check the purchase request, submit it and resolve availability or delivery exceptions

tasks.design: Configure {PROCUREMENT} to populate a request from the teacher's selected materials list in {DOCS}. The teacher retains textbook selection and checks the exact request before submission; purchasing approval remains with the purchasing team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selected catalogue details are retyped into request fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Native catalogue imports or saved request lines can reuse selected identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Edition suitability, accessibility, price changes and substitutes need judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher decides which texts support the course.
tasks.altitude: Less request transcription; no added purchasing authority.

evidence.claim: Catalogue-backed purchase requests can reuse selected item fields; the 20-hour duplicate-entry share is an E1 scenario, not a measured education case.

assumptions: Boundary is the teacher's selection and request effort through supply exceptions. Purchasing approval, ordering and supplier fulfilment stay outside and unchanged.

Teacher captures title, edition, item identifier, quantity, course code, delivery date and cost centre in s1's retained 65 hours; that produces the selected materials list. Missing identifiers or unsupported imports use manual requests in s3.
Try native catalogue and request configuration first; already automated entry earns no saving.
unknowns: Observed entry share and procurement permissions
research_questions: Does list reuse reduce actual entry without extra selection-time form filling?

incremental.description: Check request field mappings and catalogue changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact request version, editions, quantities, costs and delivery fields; edits void submission approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=80; gross 20 less 4 upkeep gives net 16. Low is a native catalogue already doing the entry with no change deployed; high requires 20 hours of observed repeated typing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Serve on academic and administrative committees

steps.what: Read committee papers and prepare a position on academic or institutional issues
Serve on committees by debating policy, voting and agreeing departmental actions

tasks.design: Keep reading and deliberation with the teacher, using the existing committee papers in {DOCS}. No secretary or meeting administration saving is assigned to this committee member.
tasks.previous_blocker: Institutional choices depend on context and representation.
tasks.enabler_now: None removes the need to understand papers and deliberate personally.
tasks.still_hard: Competing academic interests require accountable judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The member represents teaching experience and tests the consequences of policy.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in committee workload or voting rights.

evidence.claim: Preparation and committee deliberation remain personal work in this boundary; no clerical baseline is inferred.

assumptions: Boundary is an ordinary member's preparation and participation, excluding secretary duties and policy implementation.
Existing committee papers are produced by the committee secretariat upstream; their preparation is unchanged and earns no saving here. No machine step needs structured input.
No deployment or new upkeep is introduced, so incremental effort is zero.
unknowns: Actual committee duties and preparation needs
research_questions: Does the teacher hold separate secretary duties needing a separate task boundary?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100; unchanged preparation and participation with zero upkeep yields zero saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in campus and community events

steps.what: Participate in campus and community events through discussion, readings and informal exchanges

tasks.design: Keep personal event participation with the teacher. Existing programme information may remain in {DOCS}; no event-organising workload is invented for an attendee.
tasks.previous_blocker: Presence and exchange are the purpose of participation.
tasks.enabler_now: No software removes that need within this boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Conversations and relationships develop during the event.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher contributes authentic experience and responds to people present.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the teacher's event participation.

reach.task: Take part in public literary discussions

evidence.claim: Participation is human presence and exchange; no event-administration saving follows from this task statement.

assumptions: Boundary is attendance and active participation, excluding event production and marketing.
The organiser supplies the existing event programme upstream with unchanged effort. No automated step requires structured capture.
No implementation or ongoing maintenance is proposed; incremental hours are zero.
unknowns: Whether the teacher is also an organiser
research_questions: Is event planning a separate duty rather than part of participation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 and zero upkeep; unchanged participation yields zero saving.

Support instructional coordinators with policy impact assessment
